page.layout: One printed page, single column of text with a woodcut ornament band above the heading; faint show-through from the reverse side in the background (not transcribed); a Greek signature-like line at right of the dedication; catchword/signature at foot right "II. SCAN" as a signature mark.

p.i: MIRA tibi dico GRUNERE, sed optima? vera: Cùm brumale riget glaciali frigore Cœlum

l.i: Nonne ardere tuum tunc sentis ad ardua zelum?
Dùm Cœlum ningit, tua mens sublimia fingit;
Dùm corpus findit frigus, mens æthera scindit;
Frigore dùm pallet corpus, mens optuma callet;
Dùm foris furit acris hyems, mens urit & intùs;
Corpore dùm friges, animo vigesq; calesq;
Sicq; vires animo, dùm languent frigore vires
Corporis, atq; vires studiis, industria vires
Sumit; dùmq; vires, meritò te dico VIRETUM.
Mira tibi dixi, GRUNERE, sed optima, vera.

page.notes: The Greek line after "Amico amicissimo" is a Greek dedicatory phrase written at the right edge; it is not transcribed in Greek letters due to legibility. Show-through text from the reverse page is ignored. The initial M is a large woodcut-style initial, joined to "IRA" as "MIRA". Some words are doubtful: "optuma" in "mens optuma callet" may be "optima" [?]. Left-margin mark "I.AC" near the foot is a faint signature, not transcribed.
